note: SYNTHETIC. Scripted visit notes written for this hackathon. Not real patients. Read aloud by the builder to create recordings/S01..S10 (+ _noisy variants).

matching.patient.name: case-insensitive; Levenshtein distance <= 2 counts as a match (ASR spells names differently)
matching.complaint.keywords: every keyword must appear (case-insensitive) in the extracted complaint terms or their evidence text
matching.complaint.mustNotContain: none of these may appear in the extracted complaint terms
matching.complaint.durationDays: exact; null means no duration should be extracted
matching.vitals: exact numbers; temperature compared in the unit spoken; only listed vitals are scored
matching.medications: matched by canonical generic name; only the listed keys are compared
matching.mayAlsoContain: an extra medication not in the list is a false positive unless listed here and carrying the required flag
matching.referral: null means no referral should be extracted; 'to' is a case-insensitive substring match
matching.followUp: null means no valid follow-up should be extracted; 'date' is computed from visitDate
matching.flags: each expected {code, target} must appear: same code, and the produced target contains the expected target (case-insensitive). Extra flags are listed in the report, not penalised.

scripts.tests: basic clean note; number words; temperature unit inferred from range (no flag)
scripts.text: Patient Noor, thirty-eight years. Complains of fever for three days. Temperature one hundred and one. Gave paracetamol five hundred milligrams three times a day for three days. Review after three days.

scripts.tests: BP and pulse; 'once at night' timing; 'worse in the mornings' must not become a follow-up or a medicine timing
scripts.text: Patient Ramesh, fifty-two. Sneezing and runny nose for one week, worse in the mornings. BP one forty over ninety. Pulse eighty-eight. Gave cetirizine ten milligrams once at night for five days. Follow up in one week.

scripts.tests: urgent referral; 'seven months pregnant' must not become the complaint duration; unclear follow-up
scripts.text: Patient Sunita, twenty-six, seven months pregnant. Swelling of feet and headache since yesterday. BP one sixty over one hundred and ten. Referred to the district hospital today. Follow up after delivery.

scripts.tests: child; 'O R S' alias; prn medicine with no dose; two medicines; advice tags
scripts.text: Patient baby Aarav, two years, brought by mother. Loose motions since two days. Gave O R S after every loose stool, and zinc twenty milligrams once daily for fourteen days. Advised mother to continue breastfeeding and give plenty of fluids. Review in five days.

scripts.tests: spoken correction ('sorry, make that'); with food; weeks
scripts.text: Patient Lakshmi, sixty years. Pain in both knees for two months. Gave diclofenac fifty milligrams twice a day after food for five days. Sorry, make that ibuprofen four hundred milligrams twice a day after food for five days. Review in two weeks.

scripts.tests: missing follow-up (red); decimal temperature; hard drug name for ASR
scripts.text: Patient Kavita, thirty-three. Burning while passing urine for two days. Temperature ninety-nine point eight. Gave nitrofurantoin one hundred milligrams twice a day for five days. Advised to drink plenty of water.

scripts.tests: visit reason without symptoms; weight; 'continue' = ongoing (no duration needed); months
scripts.text: Patient Mohan, seventy. Came for a blood pressure check. BP one fifty over ninety-five. Weight sixty-two kilos. Continue amlodipine five milligrams once daily. Review in one month.

scripts.tests: small talk and fillers ignored; qualitative temperature; dose without unit ('six fifty'); conditional follow-up
scripts.text: Okay so, patient Imran, twenty-nine. He was saying it is very hot these days. Anyway, headache and body ache since morning. Temperature normal. Gave paracetamol six fifty, one tablet three times a day for two days. If not better, come back.

scripts.tests: negation ('No pain'); non-urgent referral; weekday follow-up resolved to a date
scripts.text: Patient Geeta, forty-one. Blurred vision for distance, slowly over six months. No pain. Referred to the eye hospital in the district for a check-up. Follow up on Monday.

scripts.tests: Celsius temperature; two medicines; prn syrup with no dose
scripts.text: Patient Raju, eight years, brought by father. Ear pain for two days. Temperature thirty-eight point two. Gave amoxicillin two hundred and fifty milligrams three times a day for five days, and paracetamol syrup when needed for pain. Review after five days.
